clue.text: Spelt and rice brewed for alcoholic drink

indicators.note: brewing stirs ingredients together into something new, so these words get mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for home-brewing booze out of a couple of grains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two grains of fodder; spelt is an ancient wheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sec is an orange-flavoured liqueur, so it is one kind of strong spirit.

clue.text: Matter of circle without radius

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the circle loses the radius letter

parts.note: the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are circles of latitude
r is the standard symbol for a radius

explanation.surface: A geometry question about a circle drawn with no radius.
explanation.walkthrough: TROPIC minus its R leaves TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The matter under discussion is its subject, which is exactly what a topic means.

clue.text: Firm on strike in Settle

parts.note: an iron will or grip is firm
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A company hit by industrial action in the Yorkshire town of Settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire; the capital S hides the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out a problem is to resolve or smooth it away, the same as to settle it.

clue.text: Lyric poem's hot on beat

parts.note: a lay is a short lyric or narrative poem
someone hot on a hobby is keen on it, or into it

explanation.surface: A song lyric praised as being strong on rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a musical rhythm but is the verb, meaning thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is to attack them physically or verbally, much as to beat them.

clue.text: Outwardly shy acknowledgement in assembly

indicators.note: outwardly points at the outside of the word, keeping only its edge letters

parts.note: the first and last letters
a nod of the head acknowledges someone

explanation.surface: A bashful person gives a small sign of recognition at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a formal council of church officials, a kind of gathering or assembly.

clue.text: Spooner's wet fool in Blitz

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: wet is damp and a fool is a clown; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A soggy idiot wandering through wartime London during the bombing.
explanation.walkthrough: DAMP CLOWN with the initial sounds swapped becomes CLAMP DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz in the sense of a concerted campaign against wrongdoing is a crackdown or clampdown.

clue.text: About about about about an emperor

indicators.note: the first About means turn around, so everything after it is read from right to left
the third about means surrounding, so the word before it goes around the word after

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone stammering helplessly, repeating one word while trying to discuss a Roman ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Every 'about' plays a different role: ON wrapped about RE makes OREN, and the leading About reverses it to NERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was the Roman emperor famous for fiddling while Rome burned.

clue.text: New suits Charlie leaves for groups of people

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the Charlie letter goes out of the word

parts.note: lawsuits are legal actions
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie walks out leaving new clothes behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' looks like clothing but means lawsuits; ACTIONS loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a large body of people united by shared history, culture or territory.

clue.text: Additional conditions limit American asset strippers

indicators.note: to limit is to bound on every side, so the conditions enclose what follows

parts.note: riders are clauses added to a contract or bill
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Extra clauses in a deal restrict US investors who break up companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate raiders buy companies to sell off their assets, so they are asset strippers.

clue.text: How Man City manager gives inspiration to his players?

definitions.text: How Man City manager gives inspiration to his players?

parts.words: How Man City manager gives inspiration to his players?
parts.note: surface reading: a football boss motivating his squad
setter's reading: Pep Guardiola, so his speeches are named after him

explanation.walkthrough: Pep Guardiola has managed Manchester City since 2016; motivating speeches carry his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousing speeches given to a team before a match are what coaches call encouraging talks, with a pun on Pep.

clue.text: Star in favour of working around Cyprus

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the working word wraps the island abbreviation

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a machine that is working is on
CY is the international code for Cyprus

explanation.surface: A celebrity keen on doing a tour of a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity, but it is a real star in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Procyon is the brightest star in the constellation Canis Minor.

clue.text: A way to travel up

parts.note: taken as written
striding is one way of getting about on foot

explanation.surface: Someone describing a route going uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like part of the journey but is the definition, as a jockey is up on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up on a horse or bike means sitting on it with a leg on each side, which is sitting astride.

clue.text: Hit opponents in gang

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the opponents go within the gang

parts.note: a crowd is a group or set of people
in bridge North and East sit as opposing players

explanation.surface: Members of a gang beat up their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge pairs are North-South against East-West, so N and E are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown someone is informal for striking them on the head, so crowned means hit.

clue.text: Defend time for judge in work

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter stands in where another was

parts.note: a project is a piece of work
T is the abbreviation for time
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A lawyer arguing a case before the bench at work.
explanation.walkthrough: In PROJECT, the J is swapped out for T.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect someone is to shield or guard them from harm, a close synonym of defend.

clue.text: Try and see alliance without leaders in difficult situation

indicators.note: without leaders means each word loses the letter at its head

parts.note: to have a shot is to try
to spot is to see
NATO is the North Atlantic military alliance

explanation.surface: A leaderless coalition trying to cope in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOT, SPOT and NATO each drop their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an awkward, controversial issue that nobody wants to handle, a tricky predicament.

clue.text: Sign of saint buried under lobby

indicators.note: in a down clue, buried under places the saint word beneath the lobby word

parts.note: a hall is an entrance lobby
St Mark the evangelist

explanation.surface: A saint's tomb lies beneath the entrance of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'buried under' puts the saint below the lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallmark is a distinctive feature or stamp of quality, so it is a telling mark or sign.

clue.text: Criminal on a charge in Alaskan port

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook is arrested and charged in an American harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is the largest city in Alaska and a major seaport on Cook Inlet.

clue.text: Hemp brought back from Douglas Island

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the letters inside are read backwards

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Cannabis smuggled home from the Isle of Man, whose capital is Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a fibre used for rope, and like hemp is a coarse plant fibre; 'hemp' loosely covers such fibres.

clue.text: Reports of many ore deposits

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the word that follows is given by its sound

parts.note: loads means a great many

explanation.surface: News of numerous mineral finds.
explanation.definitionFit: A lode is a vein of metal ore running through rock, so lodes are ore deposits.

clue.text: Artist crazy for soprano is upset and hurt

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the result reads bottom to top
for means in place of, so one piece is swapped in where the singer letter was

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French painter
mad means crazy
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A painter flies into a rage when his singer is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: In DEGAS the S gives way to MAD, and DEGAMAD read upwards is DAMAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is damaged has been harmed or injured, so the past participle matches hurt.

clue.text: Characteristic of shirt and pants and vest

wordplay.note: each of the two garment words contains only one letter T

explanation.surface: Listing the items of underwear in a clothing drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shirt' and 'pants' each have a single T, so what they share is SINGLE T.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless undershirt, which British English calls a vest.

clue.text: Abridges right wing manifestos

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the right-wing party
tracts are political or religious pamphlets

explanation.surface: An editor cuts down the policy documents of right-wing parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is the usual abbreviation for a Conservative, Britain's main right-wing party.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract a text is to shorten or condense it, which is what abridging means.

clue.text: Making fun of knitwear design …

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the raised ridged pattern on cuffs and collars

explanation.surface: Mocking a woolly jumper, leading into the laugh at the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue's surface to the one that follows; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbing is gentle teasing, and also the ridged pattern of knitted ribs on a garment.

clue.text: … laugh about direction taken by pocket

parts.note: c for circa, meaning about

indicators.note: taken by means captured inside, so the direction goes into the pocket

parts.note: a pocket on a snooker table is a hole
RT is the abbreviation for right, a direction

explanation.surface: Continuing the teasing: a chuckle about something stashed in a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The pocket is a snooker or billiards pocket, a hole in the table, not one in clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful, breathy chuckle, so it is a kind of laugh.

clue.text: Norway involved in cultural movement against remembrance

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so the country letter sits within the rest

parts.note: a meme is an idea that spreads through a culture
N is the international vehicle code for Norway
against as in leaning to or touching, as in shoulder to shoulder

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian country joining an artistic movement opposed to commemoration.
explanation.walkthrough: A meme is an idea spreading through a culture; 'against' gives TO as in standing shoulder to shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept as a reminder, so it serves as a remembrance.

clue.text: Covering on cigarette contains old paper

parts.note: tab is slang for a cigarette

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the covering wraps the old abbreviation

parts.note: a lid is a covering
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: The wrapper of a cigarette made from old paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue means the covering follows the cigarette; tab is northern British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular, small-format newspaper, and paper is everyday shorthand for a newspaper.

clue.text: Propose removing roof from farm building

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the topmost letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a stable is a farm building for horses

explanation.surface: Suggesting taking the roof off a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: STABLE loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage, to table a motion is to put it forward for discussion, so to propose it.

clue.text: Singer involved in Normandy landings

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the letters sit within the next words

parts.note: the letters spanning the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A performer who took part in D-Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is the American singer-songwriter who won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

clue.text: Algeria revised royal privileges

indicators.note: revised means altered and rewritten, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A North African country reforms the perks of its monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia originally meant the rights and prerogatives belonging to a sovereign, before it came to mean crown jewels.

clue.text: Shakespearean character heading off for British city

indicators.note: the opening letter departs and another piece takes its place

parts.note: Pistol is Falstaff's swaggering crony in the history plays
BR is an abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: An actor playing a Shakespeare role sets off for a UK city.
explanation.walkthrough: PISTOL loses its P and gains BR in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a large city and port in south-west England.

clue.text: Opening of a key appeal

parts.note: taken as written
D is a musical key
it means sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: The start of an important legal appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening of' looks like a first-letter instruction but is the definition plus link.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal entrance passage into a mine, so it is an opening.

clue.text: Maybe Holly has enduring appeal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a plant that keeps its leaves all year, holly being one example

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: having enduring appeal
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a song or star that stays popular for ever

explanation.surface: A woman named Holly remains attractive as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Holly look like a name; 'Maybe' signals it is just one example of the plant type.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly keeps its leaves through winter, and a perennially popular song or performer is also called this.
